steps.title: Weigh the relationships
steps.count: 164 arrows · 164 clear all three · 17 corroborated · 34 answered elsewhere, 3 disputed
headings: Filter iThis does not decide what you carry — clicking an arrow does, and that click is the record. What the three readings are for is finding the arrows worth declining: 164 of them is more than anyone inspects by hand, and a relationship can fail any of the three independently. Nothing is counted twice, so a relationship expensive to specify is not thereby recorded as poorly evidenced. Across the whole corpus, 57 relationships are answered by another paper — 73 edges in three verbs: a paper responding to, refining or contradicting one specific relationship in another. The count above is the part of that reaching the constructs you carry. A relationship that has been answered is marked in the list below. 3 of them are disputed: the answering paper asserts the very same statement and gives it a different sign. For those, the corroboration count above is counting an answer as independent agreement, which overstates the evidence — three papers asserting one statement are not three papers unless they arrived at it separately. Those rows are marked in red, and the count is left as it is rather than silently adjusted, because which of the two readings you want is a judgement and not a default.

Commensurability iThe two constructs a relationship joins already agree this far on level, units and time structure. At four nothing is owed, and this is the bar that binds a modeller and an empiricist alike.

Specification iThe papers settled this much about the form of the relationship: its functional form, how several antecedents combine, any moderator, the direction. At four, nothing about the form is left for you to invent.
Direction iThe same field as direction stated above, which asks only whether a direction is given. A null is a value like any other here, so it is kept rather than dropped.

Evidence iSomething stands behind the relationship: a magnitude, estimated from the paper's own data, first-hand, scope stated. It measures what is there to check, not whether the relationship is true.
Basis iThe same field as estimated from data and first-hand above, which ask only how far it goes. Every relationship carries exactly one of the four.

steps.title: Operationalize the model
steps.count: 0 of 572 choices narrowed · 0 of 75 composed · arithmetic not written
headings: Quantities iEach construct typed as a mathematical object: its kind, its aspect, its bounds.A construct as the literature reports it is a measured thing, with a level, a bearer and a scale; a quantity in a model is a mathematical object. The signature on the right is what the corpus recorded, so a field-level stock declared a firm-level degree is visible as you do it. aspect is the one that bites: a quantity measured against a baseline is zero there by construction, which is a fact about the measure and not a finding.as recorded reads the two things the corpus holds for all 422 — a scale and whether the thing is a stock or a flow — into the nine kinds. It narrows rather than settles: an ordinal stock comes back as two of nine, nominal reaches no kind the nine have a word for, and ratio says a zero is meaningful without saying what of. Aspect it cannot touch, because nothing records it — which is what differences is for, and that one proposes from the name rather than reading anything off, so it ticks what it matches and leaves the rest where it was.
Outcomes iThe mechanisms writing each outcome, and the rule that combines them.
Parameters iThe range each one is swept over.

Mechanisms iEach relation's role, and the class of shapes it runs over.The six on the left say what the relation does — and that is what makes a mechanism ablatable, since you can only switch off an operation named as separable. The six on the right are the class of shapes it will be run over, in the property vocabulary check_family() verifies. as stated reads the shape a paper committed to where one did and the estimator did not do it for them: 97 of the 1080 relationships carry a shape imposed by a method, almost all of them linear, and a regression's default is not a theory's commitment — 9 of the 164 carried here have one. A shape class is conjunctive, which inverts what a bulk action can mean: unlike the kinds on the left, every property ticked here NARROWS the class, so none is the widest declaration available and not the narrowest. monotone is as much as can be said without choosing a curvature.

Substitutes iMechanisms that stand in for each other.Declared before the run and not after it. If two mechanisms substitute, disabling either alone changes nothing, and a loop that has not been told reports that neither mattered. Any two writing the same quantity are candidates, and the corpus says how common that is rather than leaving it an assumption: 82 consequents carry two or more distinct causes from two or more independent papers, over a third of relationships.

headings: The set to explore
The findings

What each mechanism rests on iOne line per relation the curation carried: how many relationships and papers stand behind it, which signs they asserted and whether those agree, what kind of support they are, how many merely restate one sample, and how many bound nothing. The papers' own words are inside, because a scope sentence is written to sit beside its own relationship in its own paper and reads as reference material anywhere else. Read beside the regions above, never compared with them: a declared box is an interval over named parameters and a stated scope is a sentence about a population, and nothing here pretends one bounds the other.

What your findings still leave open iTwo questions, about the findings you retained on step 3.2 and no others.Two dimensions are kept apart, because a conclusion can be robust to one and fragile to the other: the class of functional forms, and the parameter setting. A finding proved over the declared box has answered the second and may not have been asked the first at all, which is the commonest state a board is in. And where the class has been run, the combinations it contradicts are the ones to read: a combination the search could not settle is not a combination that disagreed, and the two are counted apart. What is asked about here is the model you built, never the one that ships with the page.

steps.title: Share the action model
headings: The five decisions iThe same device as the chain under step 3.2: a list that counts itself, so what is missing is stated rather than inferred from its absence. Every other step on this bench exists to stop a choice being defaulted, and these five would otherwise be defaulted. Four of them are declarations, in the same shape as every other declaration here: a closed list where the choice is closed, free text where it is not, each carrying the day it was made, travelling in the project and reversible. The fifth is not a free choice and says so.

The deposit, as one file iOne archive and not six downloads, because a deposit of six downloads is six chances to ship five of them. Inside: the parts above, the five decisions with the reason for each, a CITATION.cff, and a MANIFEST.txt carrying a SHA-256 per file computed over the bytes that went in — so a reader can check that what they have is what was deposited without trusting this page or the archive it came from. The archive is stored rather than compressed and carries no timestamps, so the same deposit gives the same bytes and therefore the same digest.

The action model, part by part iAn action model is a building block somebody else can start from, and it is not one file. Each step leaves something, and a reader who disagrees with a conclusion wants the step the disagreement is about — the relationships it rests on, the declarations, the arithmetic — rather than the whole of it. Those are addressable here one at a time; the last row is all of them together, and it is the one a citation should pin to. What is not here is said so rather than left to be discovered.
